selection_detail: Standalone Tier-1d demand-driven run (dispatcher claimable buffer starved: claimable 8 < floor 36, and nearly the entire open actionable backlog is mobile-native/KMP work that is structurally unlandable in the cloud runner). Fresh landable NON-mobile-native review vectors were required, so mobile-native-kmp was excluded despite being the strict cursor-oldest at 2026-08-25. Segment coverage already produced TODAY (2026-09-03) before this run: mobile-native-kmp, ppt-web-core, ppt-web-ui, reality-web (four tier1d signal files present). Among the landable Rust/frontend segments NOT yet covered today, the backend Rust candidates api-handlers and reality-server share the oldest review_cursor date (2026-08-31); api-handlers was selected (most security-critical per the skill's fallback priority, and it holds the legally-significant governance/voting surface). Saturation check: backlog.json has only 4 OPEN + 1 ready code-review-finding rows total (none segment-tagged api-handlers), so no saturation skip. NOTE on the skill segment map: it lists the api-handlers root as backend/api-server/src/handlers/, but the real tree is backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ (workspace has servers/ and crates/ subdirs; handlers live under routes/) — root used = backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/. Primary expert = Rust, secondary = Security (per segment->expert map). Static-only sweep: unwrap/expect/todo/unimplemented across fresh (not-yet-reviewed) route files (voting/disputes/signatures/mfa/gdpr/leases/work_orders/faults/delegations/insurance/energy/meters/violations/subscriptions/messaging/outages/neighbors/my_units/unit_residents) — all production hits are safe (signatures.rs:47 expect is startup-validated ESIGN_TOKEN_SECRET; messaging.rs:2080 expect is inside #[cfg(test)]); raw-error-leak grep (`ErrorResponse::new(.., e.to_string())` and `(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, e.to_string())`); and manual authz/IDOR tracing of the voting + delegations flows from handler into the db crate (crates/db/src/repositories/vote.rs). Prior api-handlers runs mined voice_webhooks/reports/auth/ai-*/news_articles/admin/board_meetings/regional_compliance/lease_abstraction/layout/marketplace/integrations/data_residency/documents/financial/compliance/budgets/oauth/aml_dsa/rate_limit/tenant_config/listings — all deliberately avoided here. gh CLI dep-version / dependabot-history checks not applicable (no manifest files touched). All three findings are genuine, distinct, landable, non-mobile-native defects confined to a single route file or its one backing repository method; none overlaps a prior accepted finding.
note: Highest-value defect of the run is a governance-integrity authorization gap in the voting cast path: routes/voting.rs cast_vote validates unit ownership ONLY on the delegation branch and never checks that a self-voter owns the unit they name in req.unit_id, while the backing repo (vote.rs cast_vote_rls) inserts that caller-supplied unit_id with an ON CONFLICT (vote_id, unit_id) DO UPDATE SET user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id — so within one tenant an authenticated owner can cast, re-weight, or overwrite another unit's weighted ballot. Notably delegations.rs create_delegation DOES enforce the same ownership check (get_owners_rls + is_owner) that cast_vote omits, so this is an inconsistency, not a design choice. Two secondary findings: gdpr.rs returns the raw internal error string to the client on ~15 handlers (schema/info disclosure on a privacy surface), and vote_repo.update() executes its UPDATE on the raw pool with WHERE id=$1 AND status='draft' — no organization/tenant column and outside RLS (a latent cross-tenant write, currently gated only by the preceding RLS read in update_vote). All three are single-file/single-method fixes.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voting.rs:1067-1180 cast_vote (route wired POST /api/v1/voting/{id}/cast at voting.rs:47) accepts a caller-supplied req.unit_id and only gates it on `existing.is_active()`. It re-validates ownership ONLY when req.delegation_id is Some (the delegations EXISTS query at :1107-1128 binds delegate_user_id + unit_id). On the self path (delegation_id None) it builds `CastVote { vote_id: id, user_id: rls.user_id(), unit_id: req.unit_id, .. }` (voting.rs:1155-1161) with NO check that rls.user_id() owns/occupies req.unit_id.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/vote.rs:224-278 cast_vote_rls INSERTs into vote_responses using the caller-supplied unit_id and user_id verbatim, sets `vote_weight = COALESCE((SELECT ownership_share FROM units WHERE id = $3), 1.0)` (so the ballot even takes the TARGET unit's ownership weight), and uses `ON CONFLICT (vote_id, unit_id) DO UPDATE SET user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id, answers = EXCLUDED.answers, ...`. The only isolation is org-level RLS on the vote_responses insert (via rls.conn()); RLS is tenant-scoped, NOT unit-owner-scoped. Consequence: any authenticated member of the tenant can cast a ballot for a unit they do not own, and — via the ON CONFLICT overwrite — silently replace another owner's already-cast ballot for that unit, changing the weighted outcome of a legally-significant owner vote (Slovak building governance). This is ballot stuffing / vote fraud, an authorization bypass on a data-integrity-critical path.

This is an INCONSISTENCY, not an intended design: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/delegations.rs:207-233 create_delegation already enforces exactly the missing check — `state.<unit_repo>.get_owners_rls(&mut **rls.conn(), unit_id)` then `let is_owner = owners.iter().any(|o| o.user_id == auth.user_id)` returning 403 'You must be an owner of the unit ...'. The same get_owners_rls / is_owner gate belongs in cast_vote's self path before constructing CastVote. Fix: after loading `existing`, when delegation_id is None, look up owners of req.unit_id on the RLS connection and reject with 403 unless rls.user_id() is an owner (mirror delegations.rs). IG3: an integration test where user A (owner of unit U1) POSTs /voting/{id}/cast with unit_id = U2 (owned by user B) must receive 403 and leave U2's ballot untouched; it fails on main today (the insert succeeds).

Confidence high: the full call path was traced statically from the mounted route (voting.rs:47) through the handler (voting.rs:1067) into the repository INSERT (vote.rs:224). Severity high (+3): authorization bypass enabling silent tampering with weighted vote results (integrity/data-corruption on a governance surface), reachable by any authenticated tenant member.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/gdpr.rs returns the raw internal error string to the HTTP client on ~15 handler error branches via `(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, e.to_string())` — confirmed sites at gdpr.rs:63, :82, :121, :161, :213, :301, :358, :385, :425, :460, :475, :542, :601, :628 (spanning request_data_export, get_export_status, download_export, get_export_history, request_data_deletion, get_deletion_status, cancel_deletion_request, get_privacy_settings and update_privacy_settings). The `e` values are sqlx/repository errors (user_repo.find_by_id, the data-export/deletion repos, and a raw `sqlx::query(UPDATE users ...)` at gdpr.rs:619-628).

`sqlx::Error::Database(..).to_string()` renders the Postgres message, routinely including table names, column names, constraint names and SQL fragments. Returning it verbatim in the response body is a schema/information-disclosure leak to any authenticated caller who can trip a DB error — and it is especially incongruous on the GDPR/privacy surface (data export, right-to-erasure, privacy settings). It also diverges from the codebase's own safe pattern (e.g. routes/ai/voice.rs logs the detail server-side but returns a static OAUTH_EXCHANGE_FAILED_MESSAGE to the client).

Same defect CLASS as the accepted 2026-08-31 compliance.rs finding and the 2026-09-02 budgets.rs/oauth.rs findings, but a DISTINCT file not touched by any prior run. Fix: return a static generic message to the client (e.g. `(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "Failed to process privacy request")`) and add/keep a server-side `tracing::error!(error = %e, ...)` for the detail (gdpr.rs already logs audit-creation failures this way, so the pattern is present in-file). IG3: a test that forces a repo error on request_data_export / update_privacy_settings asserts the 500 body contains no SQL/schema tokens (table/column/constraint names).

Confidence medium: the `e.to_string()` client-body sites and their 500 status are confirmed by static read and are returned directly from each handler's Err arm; the exact sensitivity of the leaked string depends on which sqlx error is surfaced. Severity medium (+2): information disclosure to an authenticated caller (no auth bypass, no data loss, no crash).

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/vote.rs:737-770 `pub async fn update(&self, id, data)` runs `UPDATE votes SET ... WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'draft'` on `&self.pool` (fetch_one at the bottom). The WHERE clause filters only by primary key + status — there is NO organization_id / tenant column — and the query executes on the raw pool, so it does NOT run under Postgres RLS (unlike the RLS-scoped reads/writes in the same file that take an executor/RlsConnection, e.g. find_poll_by_id_rls and cast_vote_rls).

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voting.rs:334-395 update_vote calls this method: `state.vote_repo.update(id, data)` at voting.rs:382, with the in-file comment `// Note: update() doesn't have an RLS version yet`. Today the preceding RLS-scoped read `find_poll_by_id_rls(&mut **rls.conn(), id)` (voting.rs:342) 404s cross-tenant callers, so the non-RLS write is practically gated by that read. But the write query carries no tenant scoping of its own: any future refactor that removes, reorders, or short-circuits the read gate (or any other caller of vote_repo.update) becomes a direct cross-tenant write to another organization's vote. This matches the Rust-expert checklist item 'SQL queries (sqlx) missing a WHERE clause on tenant/owner/user ID'.

Fix: give update() an RLS variant that takes the RlsConnection executor (mirroring cast_vote_rls / find_poll_by_id_rls) so the UPDATE runs under RLS and/or add `AND organization_id = $N` to the WHERE clause, then call it from update_vote on rls.conn(); this also lets update_vote drop the separate read-then-write gate. IG3: a test where org A's manager PUTs /voting/{id} for a draft vote owned by org B asserts 404/403 and that org B's row is unchanged (with the read gate temporarily bypassed to prove the write itself is scoped).

Confidence medium: the missing tenant column and pool (non-RLS) execution are confirmed by static read; exploitation today is blocked by the handler's preceding RLS read, so this is a latent tenant-isolation gap rather than a live cross-tenant write. Severity medium (+2): tenant-isolation defense-in-depth hole on a write path, one refactor away from a cross-tenant data-integrity bug.
